identity.plain_name: A round spacer, nut or sleeve with its hole drilled off-centre: turn it with a spanner and the wheel, pulley or shaft riding on it shifts a little sideways, then clamp it so it stays put
identity.term: Eccentric adjuster (eccentric spacer, eccentric bushing or eccentric cam bolt)
aliases: eccentric nut (common 3D-printer name, e.g. on V-wheel carriages)
eccentric bushing / eccentric bush / offset bushing / eccentric sleeve
eccentric hub (bicycle rear hubs; motorcycles with single-sided swingarms)
cam bolt / camber bolt / eccentric bolt with eccentric or offset washer (car wheel alignment)
eccentric stud cam follower / eccentric type cam follower (bearing catalogues)
cam height adjustment (cabinet hinge mounting plates)
identity.one_liner: A spacer, bushing or bolt whose hole is off-centre, so turning it moves the part mounted on it sideways by up to twice the offset; you turn it until a belt, chain, wheel or gear is just right and then clamp it to lock the setting.
identity.complexity: A few parts: the eccentric itself (a round or hex-headed spacer, sleeve, plug or bolt with an off-centre bore or shank, often marked on its thin side); the axle, bolt or bearing that runs through the off-centre hole; the part being adjusted (a wheel, pulley, sprocket, bottom bracket or gear); and a clamp to lock it (a nut, pinch bolts, set screws or a wedge). Example: 'eccentric spacer, M5 bolt, V-wheel, lock nut'.
identity.how_it_works: The eccentric sits in a round hole or on a bolt and can turn about its own centre, but the part it carries sits in the off-centre hole, so as you turn it the carried part travels around a small circle whose radius is the offset (eccentricity). Half a turn takes it from one side to the other, giving a total sideways shift of twice the offset; turning further brings it back again, so unlike a normal nut it never gets 'tighter and tighter'. Once the belt, chain or wheel is at the right tightness you clamp the eccentric (nut, pinch bolt, set screws or wedge) so friction stops it turning. Because the carried part moves on an arc, it also moves slightly at right angles to the direction you want, for example an eccentric bottom bracket also changes the pedal height.

job: tighten and hold tension: takes up slack in a chain or belt, or presses rollers onto a rail
line parts up exactly: sets a wheel, bearing, gear or hinge to the right position and takes up play
join and hold: once clamped it is also the mounting for the axle or bolt it carries
finder_attributes.motion: rotate: you turn the eccentric through up to half a turn (180°) while adjusting, which shifts the carried part sideways along a short arc; none once it is clamped
finder_attributes.degrees_of_freedom: 0 once clamped. While adjusting, 1: turning the eccentric, which moves the carried part along an arc (mostly sideways, a little up or down).
special_behaviour: tensioning (takes up slack and holds): set once and clamped; it does not re-adjust itself as a belt or chain stretches (unlike a spring tensioner), so it must be reset as parts wear
motion conversion (e.g. rotary to linear): a turn of the eccentric becomes a small, finely controllable sideways movement
finder_attributes.holding_principle: friction or clamping (force-fit): a nut, pinch bolt, set screws or a wedge clamps the eccentric so it cannot turn; plus shape (form-fit): the off-centre bore holds the axle or bolt
finder_attributes.input_output: An adjuster, not a drive: a rotation of the eccentric (up to 180°) gives a sideways shift of up to twice the offset, e.g. about 0.79 mm in total for an OpenBuilds V-slot eccentric spacer, and 0.25-1.5 mm eccentricity on catalogue eccentric cam followers. The ratio is not constant: by geometry, the shift per degree is largest in the middle of the range and smallest near the two ends. Back-drivable: yes when unclamped, because a sideways load on the carried part tries to turn the eccentric; clamped, it is held only by friction, so under-tightened eccentrics can slip.
finder_attributes.removability: removable: unclamp, then slide off or unscrew; set screws can dent the eccentric so it is harder to re-set finely
finder_attributes.reuse_cycles: many times: metal eccentrics can be re-adjusted and re-used indefinitely if not corroded; printed eccentrics wear and can break at thin sections
finder_attributes.tools_needed: a spanner to turn it (10 mm for full-size OpenBuilds spacers and Ender 3 eccentric nuts, 8 mm for 'mini' spacers), plus a spanner or Allen key for the lock nut, ideally holding the eccentric with one tool while tightening the nut with another; a pin spanner (e.g. Park Tool SPA-1) for bicycle eccentric bottom brackets; a special hook spanner for motorcycle eccentric hubs; a screwdriver for cabinet hinge cams
finder_attributes.load: light to heavy depending on size: V-slot wheel spacers and hinge cams are light-duty; bicycle eccentric bottom brackets, motorcycle eccentric hubs, car camber bolts and bearing cam followers carry heavy loads (catalogue eccentric cam followers have static load ratings of kilonewtons). Strong in straight shear across the bolt or axle; the weak direction is rotation: a load pushing the carried part sideways makes a turning force on the eccentric that only the clamp's friction resists, which is why under-clamped eccentrics creep, creak or slip.
finder_attributes.adjustable: yes: that is its purpose; loosen the clamp, turn the eccentric to shift the part (total range twice the offset), and re-clamp
finder_attributes.play_and_precision: none once clamped: it is used to remove play (e.g. between V-wheels and a rail, or in a chain). Very fine adjustment, down to a fraction of a millimetre, especially near the ends of its range. Tolerates only small misalignment corrections (at most twice the offset, typically well under a few millimetres, except large bicycle and motorcycle eccentrics). The carried part moves on an arc, so there is a small unwanted shift at right angles.
finder_attributes.access_needed: one side only (blind) in most cases: V-slot spacers, cam bolts and hinge cams are turned from the head side; bicycle eccentric bottom brackets and motorcycle eccentric hubs are reached from the side of the frame or swingarm
finder_attributes.materials: Stainless steel (OpenBuilds eccentric spacers), steel (car cam bolts, cam-follower studs, cabinet hinge plates), aluminium or steel (bicycle eccentric bottom brackets and hubs), bronze or steel (industrial eccentric bushes). 3D-printed eccentrics in PETG or similar for light, low-stress uses, always with a metal bolt through them. The part around it can be metal, printed plastic, acrylic or wood; a metal eccentric spacer's collar needs a round hole of about 7.1 mm.
finder_attributes.maker_difficulty: easy to use bought ones (V-slot eccentric spacers are cheap and fit a round hole in a printed or cut plate); moderate to make your own: the off-centre hole must be accurate, which needs a lathe or careful printing, and printed ones are weak

processes: off-the-shelf part (most common: eccentric spacers, eccentric bushings, eccentric cam followers, eccentric bottom brackets, cam bolts)
3D print (FDM): design round pockets in printed plates to take bought eccentric spacers, or print light-duty eccentric spacers or bushings
CNC or lathe: turning an off-centre bore (metal eccentric bushings)
laser cut: round holes in acrylic or plywood gantry plates to take eccentric spacers
making.print_in_place: no: the eccentric is a separate part fitted onto a bolt or into a hole; a printed eccentric still needs a metal bolt and nut
making.making_tips_3d_printing: Easiest: print or cut the gantry plate or carriage with round holes that fit bought metal eccentric spacers (OpenBuilds spacers have a collar that 'fits into a 7.12mm hole'; one maker drilled acrylic plates to 7.1 mm), and use them on only one side of each set of wheels, with plain spacers on the other side. Print a hole-size test gauge first to find the right printed hole for M5 bolts and 7 mm eccentric collars on your printer (Printables 466199). Orient the printed plate so the holes are vertical (round in the XY plane) [uncertain: general practice, not from an opened page]. If you print the eccentric spacer itself, keep it for light duty: one designer notes that the neck of his printed long eccentric spacer 'is a bit weak so the spacer shouldn't be turned under the stress' (Printables 79881). Mark the thin side of a home-made eccentric as OpenBuilds does with a divot, so you always know where the offset points. Leave room for a spanner (or print a long eccentric-nut wrench, Printables 890104). Clamp it with a proper nut and washer on a metal bolt; do not rely on friction of printed plastic alone, which creeps under constant clamp load [uncertain].
making.off_the_shelf_parts: Search terms: 'eccentric spacer' (V-slot, 5 mm bore, 6 mm or 1/4 in tall, 8 mm or 10 mm hex), 'eccentric nut' (3D printer V-wheels), 'eccentric bushing' or 'eccentric bush', 'eccentric cam follower' or 'eccentric stud cam follower' (e.g. IKO CFE and CFES, THK CFH-A and CFH-AB series; brands), 'eccentric bottom bracket' (bicycles), 'eccentric hub' (singlespeed bicycles with vertical dropouts), 'camber bolt' or 'cam bolt kit' (cars), 'cam adjustable mounting plate' (cabinet hinges, e.g. Blum CLIP top, brand). Supplier catalogues also list 'locating pin with eccentric head' [uncertain: product page not opened].
rules_of_thumb: Total adjustment is twice the eccentricity: half a turn moves the carried part from one side to the other (geometry). Examples: an OpenBuilds eccentric spacer gives 'a total range of adjustment of approximately 0.79mm' (MakerTechStore, https://www.makertechstore.com/products/eccentric-spacer); THK eccentric cam followers have 0.25-1.0 mm eccentricity (https://www.thk.com/jp/en/products/other_rotary_guides/cam_follower/eccentric/); IKO CFE 0.4-1.5 mm (https://www.ikont.co.jp/eg/product/needle/ndl0603.html); IKO CFES 0.25-0.6 mm (https://www.mrosupply.com/bearings/862859_cfes16_iko-bearing/).

V-wheel carriages: turn eccentric nuts in very small steps until the wheels roll smoothly and can easily be pushed both ways but the carriage never wobbles; too tight and the wheels grind and damage themselves and the rail (3D Print Beast, https://www.3dprintbeast.com/eccentric-nuts-ender-3-v2-pro/). Over-tight V-wheels develop flat spots (FlixMySwitch video title, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I6NI7lGAv44).

Tandem front chain set with an eccentric: about 1/2 inch (12 mm) of up-and-down play halfway between the axles, checked all the way round the crank rotation (Park Tool, https://www.parktool.com/en-int/blog/repair-help/chain-tension-for-tandem-front-end); for a synchronising chain, set it taut at the tightest point of the crank rotation (Sheldon Brown, https://www.sheldonbrown.com/synchain.html).

Choose the clamp to suit the frame: pinch-bolt eccentrics are easiest to adjust but are 'normally only used on steel frames because of the risk of breaking off the ears'; set screws are simple but dent the eccentric; wedge types must be kept greased or they corrode in place (Sheldon Brown, https://www.sheldonbrown.com/synchain.html).
Cabinet hinge mounting plates with a cam give about +/-2 mm of height adjustment (Blum catalogue 2022/2023, https://publications.blum.com/2022/catalogue/en/144/).
Car camber bolts with eccentric or offset washers can change camber by up to about two degrees (Wikipedia 'Camber angle', https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camber_angle).

Setting gear backlash by turning an eccentric hub to change the centre distance shifts the tooth contact zone, can lower load capacity and efficiency, and causes start-up wear (Wikipedia 'Duplex worm', https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duplex_worm).

everyday_examples: the 'eccentric nuts' you turn with a 10 mm spanner to snug up the wheels on a 3D printer such as the Ender 3
the eccentric bottom bracket that tensions the chain or belt on a tandem, single-speed or belt-drive bicycle
cam bolts used in car wheel alignment to set camber
kitchen cabinet hinge mounting plates with a small cam screw for moving the door up or down
guidance.when_to_use: When you need a small, precise, lockable adjustment of where a wheel, pulley, sprocket, bearing or shaft sits: taking up play between rollers and a rail (V-slot carriages), setting chain or belt tension where the axles cannot slide (vertical bicycle dropouts, tandem timing chains, belt-drive bikes, motorcycles with single-sided swingarms), setting gear mesh or roller contact, or trimming alignment (car camber, cabinet doors, cam followers). It is compact, needs no slots, and holds its setting firmly once clamped.
guidance.when_not_to_use: When tension must be kept up automatically as a belt or chain stretches: use a spring-loaded tensioner. When you need more travel than about twice the offset: use a slotted mount, sliding motor plate or jacking screw. When the part must not move sideways at all while you adjust it in one direction (the eccentric moves it on an arc): use a straight slide or screw adjuster. For precise, repeatable gear backlash: an eccentric centre-distance change disturbs tooth contact, so consider anti-backlash or duplex-worm gearing. In weak, soft or printed parts under heavy load: printed eccentrics can break and plastic creeps under the clamp.
guidance.environment_limits: Corrosion can seize an eccentric in its housing: wedge-type bicycle eccentrics left unserviced 'can become corroded in place' (Sheldon Brown), and owners report having to tap stuck eccentric bottom brackets to turn them (Montague Bikes blog comments), so grease the outside of the eccentric. Vibration and cyclic load can make an under-clamped eccentric slowly turn and lose its setting [uncertain: not confirmed on an opened page]. Printed eccentrics and printed plates creep under constant clamp load, more in heat [uncertain].
guidance.safety_notes: Eccentrics set things that matter for safety, such as a car's wheel alignment, a motorcycle's chain tension or a bicycle's chain: re-tighten the clamp or pinch bolts to the maker's torque after adjusting, and check that the setting has not moved. When tightening the lock nut, hold the eccentric with a second tool so it does not turn and change the setting (VW Vortex forum, on an eccentric-mounted timing belt tensioner). A slack chain can come off [uncertain]. Pinch-bolt eccentric shells on non-steel frames risk breaking the bolt ears (Sheldon Brown).
guidance.common_failures: (1) It slips and loses tension because the clamp was not tight enough or the load keeps trying to turn it; tighten to the proper torque and hold the eccentric while tightening. (2) It is seized by corrosion and will not turn; grease it at assembly (Sheldon Brown), and free a stuck one with gentle taps rather than by forcing the spanner, as bicycle owners report (Montague Bikes blog comments). (3) Set screws dent the eccentric, making fine re-adjustment difficult (Park Tool; Sheldon Brown). (4) Over-tightened V-wheels grind or develop flat spots; back it off until the carriage just runs without wobble. (5) Confusion because a full turn returns to the start: work in small steps and watch the effect, and use the thin-side mark. (6) An eccentric bottom bracket creaks [uncertain: seen only in search results]. (7) A printed eccentric breaks at its thin neck when turned under load (Printables 79881). (8) Adjusting the eccentric also changes another dimension (pedal height, wheel toe) because it moves on an arc; check both after adjusting.
related: Belt tensioner (spring-loaded idler): keeps tension automatically as the belt stretches, instead of a set-and-lock adjustment
Eccentric cam lever (cam clamp, quick-release skewer): also uses an off-centre shape, but to clamp quickly with a lever rather than to set a position
Cam and follower: an off-centre or shaped disc that moves a follower continuously as it turns (the same geometry used for motion)
Slotted mount or jacking screw (adjustable centres): a straight, longer adjustment range; less compact
Lead screw and nut (incl. anti-backlash nut): fine straight-line adjustment with a screw
Dovetail slide with gib strip: takes up play in a slide with an adjustable strip instead of an eccentric
Kinematic coupling: locates parts exactly without any adjustment
Turnbuckle: sets tension in a rod, wire or cable by screwing
